text: Digital health technologies for AYUSH: 1) Telemedicine platforms for Ayurvedic consultation. 2) AI-powered diagnosis support based on traditional assessment (Prakriti, Nadi). 3) Mobile apps for wellness tracking, diet planning. 4) IoT devices for monitoring health parameters. 5) Blockchain for supply chain traceability. 6) Digital therapeutics combining AYUSH principles with technology. IP considerations: software patents limited in India (Section 3(k)), focus on trademark, trade secret, and hardware+software combinations.

Section 3(k) excludes 'computer programme per se' from patentability. Interpretation: Software alone not patentable; software with technical effect/hardware integration may be. CRI Guidelines (2017): consider whether invention has technical advancement, solves technical problem. For AYUSH digital: AI algorithm for Prakriti analysis — software per se (not patentable). AI system integrated with sensor hardware measuring pulse — may be patentable. Strategy: claim technical system, not algorithm alone.

AI/ML applications in AYUSH formulation development: 1) Predictive modeling for herb combinations. 2) Optimization of extraction parameters. 3) Analysis of clinical trial data. 4) Quality control through image recognition. 5) Personalized formulation based on patient data. IP challenges: algorithms not patentable per se, training data may be public. Strategy: patent resulting formulations discovered through AI (if novel), protect algorithms as trade secrets, patent hardware/software integrated systems.

IP for AYUSH mobile apps: 1) Copyright — protects code, UI design, content. Automatic, register for evidence. 2) Trademark — app name, logo, branding. Register in relevant classes. 3) Trade secret — proprietary algorithms, databases, business logic. 4) Patent — limited for software; consider if novel hardware integration. 5) Design — unique visual interface elements. App store presence also protected by platform terms. For AYUSH wellness apps: focus on trademark for brand, copyright for content, trade secret for proprietary methods.

IP for AYUSH telemedicine: 1) Platform technology — likely not patentable (software per se), protect through trade secret and copyright. 2) Brand name — trademark registration critical for recognition. 3) Content — consultation protocols, training materials, health content — copyright protected. 4) Data — patient data protected under privacy laws, not IP; anonymized datasets may be valuable trade secrets. 5) Integration with hardware (devices) — may be patentable. Comply with Telemedicine Practice Guidelines 2020.

Wearable devices for AYUSH monitoring: 1) Pulse analysis devices — measure Nadi characteristics. 2) Sleep monitors — track sleep quality per Ayurvedic principles. 3) Activity trackers — with Ayurvedic wellness algorithms. 4) Smart packaging — temperature/humidity monitoring for herb storage. IP strategy: patent the device hardware and hardware+software combination. Sensor innovations, novel measurement methods may be patentable. Data processing algorithms protect as trade secrets. Brand the device line with strong trademarks.

Blockchain applications in AYUSH: 1) Supply chain traceability — track herbs from farm to finished product. 2) Authentication — verify genuine products, combat counterfeiting. 3) Clinical trial data integrity — tamper-proof records. 4) Benefit sharing tracking — transparent ABS compliance. IP considerations: blockchain protocols are often open source; innovations may be in implementation, specific applications. Consider: trade secrets for proprietary implementations, patents for novel technical integrations, trademarks for blockchain-verified brand programs.

Health data in AYUSH digital products: 1) Personal Data Protection Bill (when enacted) will regulate health data. 2) IT Act 2000 Section 43A requires reasonable security practices. 3) Sensitive personal data rules apply to health information. 4) Patient consent required for collection, use, sharing. 5) Anonymization may allow broader use for research. IP intersection: datasets may be trade secrets, but privacy compliance constrains use. For AYUSH digital: implement privacy by design, get proper consents, document compliance.

AYUSH Grid is government initiative for digitizing AYUSH sector: 1) Digital Health Records for AYUSH. 2) Telemedicine network for traditional medicine. 3) Hospital Information Systems for AYUSH hospitals. 4) Drug licensing portal (eLIMS). 5) AYUSH Research Portal. 6) Online examination systems. IP considerations: government platforms are public infrastructure; private innovations built on or integrating with AYUSH Grid can be protected. Opportunity: develop compliant solutions that work with government systems.

Digital therapeutics (DTx) deliver therapeutic interventions through software. AYUSH DTx possibilities: 1) Yoga instruction apps with therapeutic protocols. 2) Meditation apps based on traditional techniques. 3) Cognitive behavioral interventions rooted in Ayurvedic psychology. 4) Diet management based on Prakriti. IP for DTx: clinical validation data supports regulatory and IP claims, trademark the DTx brand, copyright content/algorithms, patent novel delivery methods or integrated devices. Growing regulatory framework globally; India framework emerging.

3D printing applications in AYUSH: 1) Personalized dosage forms — tablets, capsules with custom doses. 2) Complex release profiles — multi-compartment formulations. 3) Patient-specific shapes for compliance. 4) On-demand manufacturing at point of care. IP considerations: 3D printing process patents, specific formulation designs, printer hardware innovations. CAD files for formulations may be copyrightable. Trade secrets for printer settings, material formulations. Emerging area with growing patent activity globally.

VR/AR applications for AYUSH: 1) Immersive yoga instruction. 2) Meditation environments. 3) Surgical training for AYUSH procedures. 4) Patient education — visualize treatment effects. 5) Clinic ambiance enhancement. IP protection: VR content protected by copyright, VR hardware innovations potentially patentable, branding through trademark. Integration with biometric sensors may create patentable system. Content licensing important — ensure rights to use in VR.
